name: Georgia

ga_hope_gpa.label: HOPE GPA
ga_hope_gpa.description: HOPE GPA: core courses grades 9-12 on a flat 4.0 scale; +0.5 for B-F grades in AP, IB and dual enrollment core courses; no rounding.

programs.name: HOPE Scholarship
programs.summary: Tuition help at Georgia public and eligible private colleges for students with a 3.0 HOPE GPA and 4 rigor courses.

award.summary: Per-credit-hour amount set each year by college (e.g. about $5,017 a semester at UGA in 2026-27); flat $2,985 a semester at private colleges.

programs.name: Zell Miller Scholarship
programs.summary: Full standard tuition at Georgia public colleges for students with a 3.7 HOPE GPA, 4 rigor courses and a 1200 SAT or 25 ACT.

award.summary: 100% of standard tuition at public colleges.

deadlines.title: Complete the GSFAPP on GAfutures (alternative to the FAFSA for HOPE and Zell)

aid_steps.title: Student makes a GAfutures account
aid_steps.summary: GAfutures is Georgia's site for HOPE, Zell Miller and other state aid. The student's account shows their HOPE GPA and state awards.
how: Open GAfutures and choose Create an Account.
Use the student's own email. The site asks for the Social Security number and date of birth so it can match high school records.
Pick a username (6 to 49 characters) and a strong password, and save them somewhere safe at home.
watch_out: Never type the GAfutures password or Social Security number into ScholarTasks.

aid_steps.title: GSFAPP, only if you are not filing the FAFSA
aid_steps.summary: Georgia accepts either the FAFSA or its own short form, the GSFAPP, for HOPE, Zell Miller and other state programs. Filing the FAFSA is enough; the GSFAPP is for families who choose not to file the FAFSA.
how: If you filed the FAFSA, mark this step Doesn't apply.
Otherwise sign in to GAfutures and complete the GSFAPP for the year you start college.
The deadline is the last day of the college term (or the day you withdraw), but apply early so money reaches the college sooner.
watch_out: The GSFAPP does not give federal aid such as Pell Grants or federal loans. Only the FAFSA does.

aid_steps.title: Check the HOPE GPA on GAfutures
aid_steps.summary: High schools send grades to the Georgia Student Finance Commission, which works out the official HOPE GPA. Compare it with the estimate on your ScholarTasks Grades page.
how: Sign in to GAfutures and open the HOPE GPA section of your account.
Compare it with the ScholarTasks Grades page. A big difference usually means a class was coded differently. Ask the school counselor.
Check again after senior grades are final. HOPE and Zell are decided from the final record.

aid_steps.title: Make sure HOPE or Zell shows on your aid offer
aid_steps.summary: Once the FAFSA or GSFAPP is on file, the Georgia college adds HOPE or Zell Miller to the aid offer. If it's missing, ask.
how: Look for HOPE Scholarship or Zell Miller Scholarship on the chosen Georgia college's aid offer.
If it's missing, contact the college's financial aid office and check your GAfutures account.
Remember HOPE is kept by keeping a 3.0 college GPA (Zell: 3.3), checked at set points.

link.label: HOPE: how to apply and deadlines

counselor_notes: Georgia accepts the FAFSA or its own short form, the GSFAPP, for HOPE and Zell Miller; only the FAFSA gives federal aid. HOPE needs a 3.0 HOPE GPA and Zell Miller a 3.7 plus a 1200 SAT or 25 ACT from a single sitting; both need 4 rigor courses. HOPE is kept with a 3.0 college GPA (Zell: 3.3), checked at set points. GAfutures (gafutures.org) shows the official HOPE GPA. HOPE and Zell only pay at Georgia colleges.

verification.note: DRAFT from third-party summaries. Every rule, amount and date must be verified with GSFC before this pack moves to review. GSFC's rigor-course list is broader than AP/IB/DE (it also names some advanced math, science and foreign-language courses); model that before beta.
